static_traits.name: Zhang Chen
static_traits.social_status: Having supportive friends and family willing to Listening, but not fully understanding the degree of driving-related Anxiety; avoiding social activities involving driving has affected Interpersonal relationships.
static_traits.medical_history: Experienced a second car accident two years ago, had physical injuries and was in Recovery; No major physical illness; no similar psychological problems before, no psychotherapy received before.
static_traits.language_features: Clear and organized expression, able to describe trigger situations and automatic thoughts specifically; highly cooperative, Positive attitude; capable of self-observation, but with tendencies toward catastrophizing, predicting the future, and overgeneralization.

basic_info.main_problem: I keep having the thought 'I will soon get into another car accident'; these thoughts trigger Anxiety and Fear, and gradually lead me to Avoids driving or riding in cars as much as possible, affecting Learning, social life, and daily life.
basic_info.core_demands: Because driving-related Fear and Anxiety affect academic performance and social life, hoping to reduce the impact of these thoughts and emotions through counseling and Recover daily functioning.
growth_experiences: The client has had two car accidents (the most recent two years ago); after the second accident he entered a recovery period for physical injuries, and stress rose markedly; since then he began persistently worrying about another car accident occurring; seeing cars or thinking about driving triggers strong fear, and he gradually avoids driving or riding in cars, leading to declining academic performance, reduced social activities, and daily affairs being affected.

core_beliefs: Bad things (disasters) will happen to me again
I cannot guarantee my driving safety

special_situations.event: Seeing cars on the road or thinking about driving
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I drive, a serious car accident will almost certainly happen again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding driving or riding in cars as much as possible
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will have another car accident soon; may be seriously injured or worse

special_situations.event: As commute or travel time approaches
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: The closer the travel time, the higher the danger; I cannot ensure my safety on the road
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Postponing or canceling trips, switching to other means or simply not going out
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Something bad will happen to me going out this time

special_situations.event: Hears news about car accidents or others recounting accidents
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Others having a car accident means I am also very likely to encounter the same accident
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids related topics and information sources
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Since others also get into accidents, I will run into one sooner or later

special_situations.event: Recalls the second car accident two years ago and the injury recovery experience
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Having had two car accidents means I am destined to be unsafe
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Maintaining high vigilance, avoiding driving practice or activities requiring driving
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am so afraid, which shows driving is dangerous

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be protected and stay safe, avoiding being hurt again or having a car accident
core_conflict.fear: Fearing loss of control, getting injured again, or even Death
defense_goal: Maintaining a sense of safety by Avoiding driving and riding in cars
High vigilance and preemptive avoidance of possible risks

object_relations.object_representation: Roads and other drivers are seen as potential threats / a dangerous environment
Family and friends are well-meaning but not fully understanding others

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor suggests a graded behavioral experiment (short-distance driving) to test catastrophized predictions
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Understands gradual exposure as putting oneself at high risk, worrying something will happen again
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing worry in a cautious, restrained tone, requesting smaller, more controllable steps and safety contingency plans.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing the negative impact of Avoiding driving on academics and social life
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Views avoidance behavior as a necessary and legitimate safe choice
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Emphasizes 'safety is the most important' in a calm but firm tone, defending continued avoidance on the grounds of safety.

manifestations: Frequently worries about another serious car accident, serious injury, or worse
When hearing car accident information, associates it with her own high risk
Limits travel and social participation to avoid driving or riding in cars
Fear intensifies before commuting and travel, restricting behavior
Although having family and friends' support, they do not fully understand the degree of Anxiety
Feeling misunderstood amid worry and fear

positive_force: Having a supportive network of family and friends
Positive attitude, willing to try new strategies and behavioral experiments
Able to identify and describe trigger factors and negative automatic thoughts
The fact of having driven safely many times without accidents serves as counter-evidence (client's own account)
negative_force: Cognitive patterns of catastrophizing, predicting the future, and overgeneralization
Strong avoidance of driving / riding in cars
Anticipatory Anxiety rises significantly before commuting and traveling
Sense of safety depends on avoidance strategies, limiting functional recovery

target_behavior.behavior: Intense fear of and avoidance of driving or riding in cars
target_behavior.core_reason: Two car accident experiences (the most recent one two years ago) triggered catastrophizing about another accident and overestimation of risk, forming the automatic belief that 'an accident will inevitably happen again'
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential danger and reducing anxious feelings
target_behavior.consequence: Declining academic performance, Interpersonal relationships affected, daily activities and errands disrupted or restricted
